entry.name: mc.zigzag~
entry.description: Use zigzag~ to generate multisegment linear ramps. This object is similar to line~, but retains information about the ramp after it has been output, and allows modification of the list values for the ramp.

arguments.name: initial-value
arguments.description: Sets an initial value (y) for theobject.

attributes.name: loopmode
attributes.digest: Enable looping
attributes.description: The word, followed by 1, turns on looping.turns off looping. By default, looping is off.turns on looping in "pendulum" mode, in which the value and time pairs are traversed in an alternating forward and reverse direction. By default, looping is off

attributes.name: maxpoints
attributes.digest: Maximum-line points
attributes.description: Specifies the number of user-defined points for ramps. The defualt value is 2048.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Specify how theobject responds to messages and signal values
attributes.description: specifies the way that theobject responds to messages and signal values.mode 0 (default): When theobject receives a, it will jump to the start point (or end point if our direction is negative) and begin outputting values from there. The time value associated with this jump has its length defined by themessage. The default value foris. If a signal is connected to the left inlet of theobject in this mode, the current index of the list is determined by the signal; any previously set,,, andmessages are ignored.mode 1: behavior is exactly the same as in mode 0 in terms of the effect of a. In mode 1, signal inputs are handled differently. If a signal is connected to the left inlet of theobject in mode 1, the input signal functions as a trigger signal; when the slope of the input signal changes from non-negative to negative, the object will be re-triggered as though awere received.mode 2: jump to the next index in the list (or the previous index, if the current direction is negative) and begin outputting values from there. The time value associated with this jump has its length defined by themessage. The default value foris. If a signal is connected to the left inlet of theobject in mode 2, the input signal functions as a trigger signal; when the slope of the input signal changes from non-negative to negative, the object will be re-triggered as though awere received.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Append new event pair(s)
messages.description: The word append, followed by a list, will add new (value) (ramp-time) pairs to the end of the current list. Sending anmessage will immediately trigger a ramp only made of the new points.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Function depends on mode setting
messages.description: In left inlet: Theobject responds to amessage according to its mode of behavior, which is set using themessage.If theobject is set to mode 0 or mode 1, amessage will cause theobject to go to the start point (or end point if the direction is negative) and begin outputting values from there.If theobject is set to mode 2, amessage will cause theobject to jump to the next index in the list (or the previous index, if the current direction is negative) and begin outputting values from there.

messages.name: bangdelta
messages.digest: Set the transition time when a bang is received
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by aor, specifies the time over which the transition between values occurs when theobject receives a. The default is 0 (i.e., and immediate transition).

messages.name: bound
messages.digest: In left inlet: The word, followed by two numbers which specify start and end indices (where 0 is the first element), sets the start and end points of theobject's linked list
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by two numbers which specify start and end indices (where 0 is the first element), sets the start and end points of theobject's linked list.

messages.name: delete
messages.digest: Delete an index/value pair
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element), will delete the value and time pair associated with that index from the list. Acan follow themessage if you want to remove multiple event pairs from the list. The messagewill remove the current first value and time pair from the list; the second value and time pair (i.e. the value and time pair at index 1) will now become the first values in the list.

messages.name: dump
messages.digest: Output all currently stored value and time pairs
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordwill cause a list consisting of all currently stored value and time pairs in the formto be sent out theobject's 3rd outlet.

messages.name: end
messages.digest: Set the point where theobject ceases output when triggered by a
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element), sets the point at which theobject ceases its output when triggered by a.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: Each element in theobject's linked list is a pair that consists of a target value (y), followed by a second number that specifies a total amount of time in milliseconds (delta-x). In that amount of time, numbers are output regularly in a line from the current index value to the target value. The listdescribes a line which begins with a value of 0 at time 0, rises to a value of 3.5 a half second later, and rises again to a value of 10 in 1 second.In right inlet: Specifies the rate at which the value and time pairs will be output. A value of 1.0 traverses the list forward at normal speed. A playback rate of -1 traverses the list backwards (i.e. in reverse). A value of .5 traverses the linked list at half the normal speed (effectively doubling the delay time values).

messages.name: insert
messages.digest: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element)
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element) and a list, will insert new event pair(s) before the index specified. The messagewill create a new first entry in the linked list (at the 0 index) with a value of 5 and a time of 500 milliseconds.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: Converted to float.In right inlet: Specifies the rate at which the value and time pairs will be output. A value of 1.0 traverses the list forward at normal speed. A playback rate of -1 traverses the list backwards (i.e. in reverse). A value of .5 traverses the linked list at half the normal speed (effectively doubling the delay time values).(In left inlet: Converted to float.)

messages.name: jump
messages.digest: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element), skips to that point in the linked list and begins outputting value and time pairs from that point
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element), skips to that point in the linked list and begins outputting value and time pairs from that point. An optional int can be used to specify the time, in milliseconds, over which the transition to the next value will occur (the default value is).

messages.name: jumpend
messages.digest: Jump forward to the last linked list value
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordcauses theobject to immediately jump forward to the last value (y)on the linked list.

messages.name: jumpstart
messages.digest: Jump to the first linked list value and output the currently selected list or selected portion of the list
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordcauses theobject to immediately jump to the first value (y)on the linked list and then output the currently selected list or selected portion of the list.

messages.name: line
messages.digest: Set breakpoints in line~ format
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list of breakpoints in line~ format (as output by theobject) defines a ramp for. The list should consist of alternating value, time pairs.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Defines and triggers a ramp
messages.description: Sets and triggers a function as (value) (ramp-time) pairs to define points in a ramp. Sending amessage will immediately trigger the ramp.

messages.name: next
messages.digest: Skip to the next value and time pair in the linked list
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordskips to the next value and time pair in the linked list. An optionalcan be used to specify the time over which the transition to the next value will occur (the default value is).

messages.name: prev
messages.digest: Skip to the previous value and time pair in the linked list
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordskips to the previous value and time pair in the linked list. An optionalcan be used to specify the time over which the transition to the previous value will occur (the default value is).

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Print status and contents of the object in the Max Console
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordcauses the current status and contents of theobject to be printed out in the Max Console. The output consists of the current mode, loopmode, the start, end, and loop length of the current list, the pendulum state, and moving value of the object, followed by a listing of each index in the linked list, along with its y and delta-x values.

messages.name: ramptime
messages.digest: Set the ramp time for output signal
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, sets the ramp time, in milliseconds, at which the output signal will arrive at the target value.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Set ramps without triggering them
messages.description: Prepending the wordto user-defined value andmessages allows for settingramps without triggering playback.

messages.name: setindex
messages.digest: Set the value and transition time for an index
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element) and a pair of floats, sets the target value (y) and transition time amounts (delta-x) for the specified position in the list.

messages.name: setline
messages.digest: Set breakpoints in line~ format without triggering them
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list of breakpoints in line~ format (as output by theobject) defines a ramp forwithout triggering it. In order to trigger the ramp, a bang needs to be sent to the first inlet. The list should consist of alternating value, time pairs.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: Theobject responds to signal values according to its mode of behavior, which is set using themessage.If theobject is set to, the current index of the list is determined by the input signal value; any previously set,,, andmessages will be ignored.If a signal is connected to the left inlet of theobject in, the input signal functions as a trigger signal; when the slope of the input signal changes from non-negative to negative, the object will be re-triggered as though awere received.If a signal is connected to the left inlet of theobject in, the input signal functions as a trigger signal; when the slope of the input signal changes from non-negative to negative, the object will be re-triggered as though awere received.In right inlet: A signal value specifies the rate at which the value and time pairs will be output. A value of 1.0 traverses the list forward at normal speed. A playback rate of -1 traverses the list backwards (i.e. in reverse). A signal value of .5 traverses the linked list at half the normal speed (effectively doubling the delay time values). The value of the input signal is sampled once per input vector. Therefore, any periodic frequency modulation with a period which is greater than the current sample rate/(2*vector_size) will alias.

messages.name: skip
messages.digest: Skip indices in theobject's linked list
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a positive or negative number, will skip the specified number of indices in theobject's linked list. Positive number values skip forward, and negative values skip backward. An optional integer can be used to specify the time over which the transition to the next or previous value will occur (the default value is).

messages.name: speed
messages.digest: Set the output rate for value and time pairs
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a positive or negative floating-point number, specifies the rate at which the value and time pairs will be output. The messagetraverses the list forward at normal speed,traverses the list backwards,traverses the linked list at half the normal speed (effectively doubling the delay time values).

messages.name: start
messages.digest: Set the point where theobject starts output when triggered by a
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by anwhich specifies a position (where 0 is the first element), sets the point at which theobject begins its output when triggered by a.

messages.name: stop
messages.digest: Stops the ramp at the current position
messages.description: Sending themessage causes the ramp to stop at the current position.
